title: Tensor-core GEMM: WMMA, then mma.sync
brief: Map each m16n8k16 lane to its elements, count a warp tile's registers, and check ldmatrix bank conflicts on the CPU. Then write a bf16 GEMM with fp32 accumulation, first with WMMA, then with ldmatrix and mma.sync, and report TFLOP/s against torch.matmul.
hints: fragment_cell is the first function. Lane 5 on A has g = 1 and t = 1, so it holds rows 1 and 9, columns 2 and 3, then columns 10 and 11. On C, elements 0 and 1 stay on row g, and elements 2 and 3 stay on row g + 8.
warp_tile_registers divides the tile across 32 lanes. A 64 by 32 tile is 64 accumulator registers, 16 A registers, and 8 B registers. A 16 by 8 tile is 4, 4, and 2.

ldmatrix_byte: lane l addresses row (l mod 8) of matrix floor(l / 8). With the 8-row swizzle, chunk c of row r moves to c XOR (r mod 8). Lane 1 at stride 64 moves from byte 128 to byte 144. Ignoring that swizzle leaves an 8-way bank conflict.

The first run compiles CUDA with nvcc, which takes 30 to 60 seconds. Later runs reuse the cached build. On a machine with no CUDA GPU the kernel checks print a skip line, and the CPU checks still grade.
The wrapper pads M and N to multiples of 128 and K to multiples of 32 with zeros, so the kernels need no bounds checks. Zero rows and columns add nothing to the dot products.

WMMA: fragments are opaque. Declare the accumulators, fill them with 0, then per 16-wide slice of K call load_matrix_sync for A and B and mma_sync. The leading dimension is the shared-memory row stride, 40 for A and 136 for B.

ldmatrix gives each thread a piece of an 8x8 matrix of 16-bit values. With .x4, lane l supplies the row address of matrix l / 8, row l % 8. For A, matrices 0 to 3 are: rows 0-7 and k 0-7, rows 8-15 and k 0-7, rows 0-7 and k 8-15, rows 8-15 and k 8-15.
B sits in shared memory as [k][n], but mma.sync wants it 'col', so load it with ldmatrix.trans. The lane-to-address rule is the same as for A.
In the C fragment, lane = 4 * g + t holds rows g and g + 8, columns 2t and 2t + 1, in four fp32 registers: c0 and c1 in row g, c2 and c3 in row g + 8.
A kernel that does not beat the 19.5 TFLOP/s fp32 CUDA-core peak is not using the tensor cores. Check the PTX type strings: .bf16 for the inputs, .f32 for the accumulator.
